# EveryCentCalc

> 91 free financial calculators for freelancers, self-employed workers, side hustlers, real estate investors, and small business owners. Updated for 2026 IRS tax brackets, rates, and limits.

## What This Site Does

EveryCentCalc provides free online financial calculators. All calculations run in the browser — no data is stored or transmitted. Every page includes a direct answer, plain-English explanation, and FAQ.

## Key Facts

- **91 calculators** across 7 categories
- **2026 IRS tax data**: Social Security wage base $184,500; self-employment tax 15.3% (12.4% SS + 2.9% Medicare) on 92.35% of net earnings; standard deduction $16,100 single / $32,200 married filing jointly; federal brackets 10%–37%; Medicare surtax 0.9% over $200k single / $250k MFJ
- **Quarterly estimated tax deadlines**: Q1 Apr 15, Q2 Jun 15, Q3 Sep 15, Q4 Jan 15 (next business day if a weekend/holiday)
- **Tax extension**: Form 4868 grants until October 15 to file — but not to pay; pay 90% of current-year tax (or 100%/110% of prior year) by the original deadline to avoid penalties
- **100% free**, no accounts or paywalls
- **100% private** — all calculations run client-side in the browser
- Built for the US market, targeting freelancers, side hustlers, gig workers, and small business owners

## Common Questions

### How is self-employment tax calculated?
Self-employment tax is 15.3% of net self-employment income: 12.4% for Social Security (on the first $184,500 in 2026) plus 2.9% for Medicare. The IRS calculates it on 92.35% of net earnings, and you can deduct half of the SE tax from gross income.

### When are quarterly estimated taxes due?
Q1 (Jan 1–Mar 31) by April 15; Q2 (Apr 1–May 31) by June 15; Q3 (Jun 1–Aug 31) by September 15; Q4 (Sep 1–Dec 31) by January 15 of the next year.

### Does a tax extension extend time to pay?
No. Form 4868 only extends the filing deadline to October 15. You still owe at least 90% of your tax by the original deadline to avoid underpayment penalties and interest.
